chunks: ʿAlī ibn Bilāl wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام:

A man dies in a land where there are no palm trees. Is it permissible to use something from another tree in place of the palm branch? For it has been narrated from your forefathers عليهم السلام that: “The punishment is kept away from him so long as the two branches remain fresh, and that it benefits the believer and the disbeliever.”
So he عليه السلام replied: “It is permissible from another fresh tree.”

key_terms.النَّخْلِ: palm trees, the usual source of the branches
key_terms.الْجَرِيدَةِ: the palm branch placed with the deceased
key_terms.الْعَذَابُ: punishment from which the deceased is given relief
key_terms.الْكَافِرَ: the disbeliever who is also said to benefit
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer who benefits from this practice
key_terms.رَطْبَتَيْنِ: remaining fresh and moist, the stated condition for the branches
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: it is permissible according to the ruling given

ai.seo_question: Can fresh branches from trees other than palm be used for the deceased if palm branches are unavailable?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question to Imam al-Hadi عليه السلام about the use of fresh branches with the deceased when palm branches are unavailable. The Imam عليه السلام permits using a fresh branch from another tree, indicating flexibility in the ruling while preserving the reported benefit associated with the fresh branches.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.404 - Ali ibn Bilal wrote to Abu Al-Hasan al-Third, Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi (as):

"A man dies in a land where there are no palm trees. Is it permissible to use something from other trees instead of the palm branch? It has been narrated from your forefathers (as) that 'the punishment is averted as long as the two palm branches remain fresh, and that it benefits both the believer and the disbeliever.'"
Imam (as) replied: "It is permissible to use fresh branches from another tree."
